_comment: The single arcade registry. The cabinet grid at /arcade reads this; the slug must match public/arcade/<slug>/ and the key in workers/arcade/games/index.js.

games.title: Swerve Valley
games.tagline: Five cellar doors. One bus. Nobody is sitting down.
games.blurb: A wine tour on an open-top bus with up to eleven friends, one phone each. One of you drives each leg — round the bends, past the roos, the right way at the fork and onto the line in the car park — while everyone in the back catches bottles, leans into corners and smiles for photos. At every cellar door you pick your pour and play the winery's game. The drunker the bus gets, the harder it is to drive, and the keys always go to whoever is soberest.

games.title: Devil's Ivy
games.tagline: Two vines, one kitchen. Never stop, only steer — and don't touch a vine.
games.blurb: You are a pothos vine loose in a real kitchen. You never stop growing and you can't slow down; all you can do is steer. Creep up the cupboards, over the ledge, across the ceiling, down the fridge and over the shopping bags while your friend does the same. Touch any vine, even your own, and you wilt. Race for the sun drops, sprint on dew, and box each other in.

games.title: Summit Fever
games.tagline: Three friends, one mountain, every kind of weather. Carry a cookie.
games.blurb: Five stages from the pines to a 4,012 m summit while the sky throws everything at you: rain, lightning, fog, gales, blizzards and a whiteout. Warmth is your lifeline, wet clothes freeze, and a cookie in your pocket is the only thing between you and hypothermia. The party only moves on when everyone reaches camp, so somebody is always going back down for a friend.

games.title: Southern Lights
games.tagline: Two friends, one headland, and something over the water.
games.blurb: You are sitting on the rocks somewhere south of Perth with a pair of binoculars between you. Lights keep appearing over the Indian Ocean. One of you works the glass, the other works the instruments, and neither of you can see the whole picture alone. Military? Mundane? Or the other thing?
